  8|
  9|“화가 나는군요.”
 10|
 11|평소 이렇게까지 노골적인 감정 표현을 하지 않는 그다.
 12|
 13|가만히 쭈그리고 있던 임꺽정이 잔뜩 궁금한 표정으로 물었다.
 14|
 15|“최 팀장, 왜 그래? 무슨 문제라도 있어?”
 16|
 17|“있습니다. 커다란 문제가.”
 18|
 19|입술을 질끈 깨문 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
 20|
 21|“이 아름다운 제품의 공급이 적다는 것. 이것이야말로 전 세계인에게 지탄받아 마땅한 가장 큰 문제죠.”
 22|
 23|“……아.”
 24|
 25|“보십시오. 고드름을 표현한 이 예술적인 자태를! 설원의 냉기를 고스란히 간직한 마법 기능을!”
 26|
 27|북한 TV 아나운서처럼 열렬하게 수령님, 아니 목걸이를 찬양하던 최 팀장이 나를 향해 고개를 홱 돌렸다.
 28|
 29|“진태경 씨는 어떻게 생각하십니까?”
 30|
 31|“저요?”
 32|
 33|어디서부터 어떻게, 그리고 뭐라 말해야 할까.
 34|
 35|고민은 짧았다. 나 자신도 놀랄 만큼 침착하고 부드러운 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 36|
 37|“저도 화가 나네요.”
 38|
 39|“…….”
 40|
 41|“왜 그러세요?”
 42|
 43|“아닙니다, 그냥.”
 44|
 45|묘한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
 46|
 47|“왠지 좀. 낯선 느낌이 들어서요.”
 48|
 49|“그래요?”
 50|
 51|턱을 문질렀다. 슬슬 고개를 내밀기 시작한 수염이 까슬까슬하다. 그 감촉이 마치 남의 살처럼 낯설었다.
 52|
 53|“면도를 안 해서 그런가.”
 54|
 55|“진태경 씨, 혹시…….”
 56|
 57|최 팀장이 뭐라 말하려던 그때, 원명훈이 사람 좋은 웃음을 지으며 다가왔다.
 58|
 59|“이야, 대단한데. 태경이 너, 진짜 잘 싸우더라.”
 60|
 61|“……그래요?”
 62|
 63|“창술 보니까 내가 만든 교본이랑은 완전히 딴판이던데. 훈련소에서 배운 거야?”
 64|
 65|“아뇨. 그냥 이것저것.”
 66|
 67|“이것저것? 그 정도 수준이 아니던데, 뭘. 이거 몇 년 후면 너한테 따라잡히는 거 아닌지 모르겠다. 하하.”
 68|
 69|나는 말 없이 입꼬리를 끌어 올렸다.
 70|
 71|아무도 따라 웃지 않자 웃음소리는 천천히 사그라졌다. 무안할 법도 한데, 원명훈은 자연스럽게 화제를 돌렸다.
 72|
 73|그런 일련의 모습들이 TV 속 드라마 장면처럼 군더더기 없이 매끄러웠다.
 74|
 75|“그런데 뭐 하고 있었어?”
 76|
 77|입은 묻고 있지만 두 눈동자는 이미 사실 파악에 여념이 없다. 최 팀장이 쥐고 있는 [예티의 목걸이]에 그의 시선이 언뜻 스쳤다.
 78|
 79|“빌려주신 목걸이 구경하고 있었어요. 최 팀장님이 이런 거에 관심이 많으셔서.”
 80|
 81|“팀장님이? 하긴. 그럴 것 같긴 하더라.”
 82|
 83|원명훈이 화려한 명품으로 온몸을 휘감고 다닌다면 최 팀장은 그 반대다.
 84|
 85|명품은 명품인데, 고급지면서도 깔끔하다고 해야 하나? 어쨌건 평소 입고 다니는 것만 봐도 이쪽에 관심이 많다는 걸 모를 수가 없다.
 86|
 87|하지만 원명훈의 관심은 다른 곳에 있었다.
 88|
 89|“그래서, 살펴보시니 어떻던가요?”
 90|
 91|최 팀장이 대답했다.
 92|
 93|“직접 보니 훨씬 좋네요. 혹시 나중에 판매 의향 있으시면 연락 주십시오.”
 94|
 95|“아쉽지만 그럴 일은 없을 것 같군요. 개인적으로 많이 아끼는 물건이라서.”
 96|
 97|개인적으로 많이 아끼는 물건이라…….
 98|
 99|그의 말을 곱씹던 내가 불쑥 입을 열었다.
100|
101|“중요한 물건인가 보네요.”
102|
103|“그럼, 아주 중요하지.”
104|
105|“그러시구나.”
106|
107|나는 원명훈을 향해 [예티의 목걸이]를 내밀었다.
108|
109|“지금 돌려드릴게요.”
110|
111|“응?”
112|
113|“형한테 중요한 물건이라면서요. 최 팀장님 말씀 들어 보니까 가격도 아주 비싼 것 같던데.”
114|
115|“…….”
116|
117|“안 받으세요?”
118|
119|손에 들린 목걸이가 흔들리며 쩔그럭 금속음이 났다.
120|
121|아주 잠깐의 침묵이 흐르고. 나를 물끄러미 바라보던 원명훈의 입가에 희미한 웃음이 맺혔다.
122|
123|“태경아.”
124|
125|“네.”
126|
127|“형은 말이다. 물건보다는 사람 간의 인연을 더 중요하게 생각해.”
128|
129|“사람 간의 인연.”
130|
131|“그래. 오늘 같이 온 길드원들도 마찬가지야. 내가 가장 힘들었던 시기에 함께 있어 준 사람들이거든.”
132|
133|“8년 전 그때 말인가요?”
134|
135|“……뭐, 그렇지. 어쨌든 형이 말하고 싶은 건, 너무 신경 쓰지 말라는 거야. 그깟 목걸이가 뭐 얼마나 소중하다고. 안 그래?”
136|
137|원명훈이 커다란 손바닥으로 내 어깨를 툭툭 두드렸다. 나와는 다르게 그의 손바닥은 부드러웠고 손톱은 길었다.
138|
139|문득 그런 생각이 든다. 어쩌면 눈앞의 이 사람은 내가 알던 그가 아닐지도 모르겠다는.
140|
141|“예티의 목걸이, 사실 그거 선물이야.”
142|
143|“선물이요?”
144|
145|“그래. 형이 너한테 주는 선물.”
146|
147|원명훈이 내게로 몸을 가까이할 때마다 독한 향수 냄새가 풍긴다.
148|
149|“그러니까 아무한테도 주면 안 된다. 알았지?”
150|
151|“…….”
152|
153|“태경아?”
154|
155|나는 목걸이를 걸며 대답했다.
156|
157|“네. 아무도 손 못 대게 할게요.”
158|
159|띠링.

163|- [예티의 목걸이]를 장착하셨습니다.
164|
165|- 목걸이에서 설원의 바람이 흘러나옵니다.
166|
167|
168|
169|전신을 휘감는 설원의 바람을 느끼며, 나는 불과 5분 전에 보았던 아이템 정보 창을 떠올렸다.
170|
171|
172|
173|아이템창
174|
175|
176|
177|[예티의 목걸이]
178|
179|종류 : 장신구
180|
181|등급 : 절정
182|
183|제한 : 없음
184|
185|설명 : 매우 뛰어난 전사 예티만이 소유할 수 있는 목걸이. 그러나 사실은 과거 용족(龍族)의 노예이자 식용 가축임을 증명하는 족쇄이다. 이 물건을 소유하고 있는 자는 종족에 상관없이 용족 몬스터의 표적이 된다.
186|
187|효과 : [설원의 바람] 효과 발동
188|
189|
190|
191|
192|
193|‘표적이라.’
194|
195|결코 유쾌한 단어는 아니다.
196|
197|여러모로.
198|
199|

201|* * *
202|
203|
204|
205|게이트에서의 시간은 느리게 흘렀다.
206|
207|꼬박 한나절 간의 이동 끝에 밀림을 벗어나 황무지에 접어들었지만, 지금껏 마주친 몬스터라고는 가장 처음 나타난 그린 와이번과 내가 처리한 오크 무리.
208|
209|그리고 지금 다른 이들이 상대하고 있는 트롤이 전부였다.
210|
211|- 그워어어어!
212|
213|성인 남성보다 머리 하나 정도 큰 키에 비정상적으로 커다란 머리.
214|
215|트롤은 재생력이 매우 뛰어난 몬스터다. 약방의 감초처럼 힐링 포션의 주재료로 쓰이는 이유이기도 했다.
216|
217|팔과 다리를 잘라 내도 불과 몇 초 만에 재생시키는 놈이니 상대하기가 까다로울 수밖에.
218|
219|그러나 스타 길드원들도 만만치 않은 베테랑들이었다.
220|
221|“머리! 머리를 노려!”
222|
223|“화염 마법!”
224|
225|서걱! 화르르륵!
226|
227|대격변 초창기에는 불사(不死)의 괴물로 악명을 떨쳤지만 트롤의 약점은 금방 들통났다.
228|
229|‘머리와 심장. 거기에 더해 마법.’
230|
231|언데드 몬스터가 아닌 이상 숨이 끊기면 죽는 것은 당연지사.
232|
233|트롤은 머리와 심장도 복구시킬 만큼 가공할 만한 재생력을 지녔지만, 그렇다고 해서 불사의 괴물까지는 아니었다.
234|
235|재생하기 전에 얼음으로 얼리거나 화염으로 지져 버리면 놈들로서도 별다른 방법이 없는 것이다.
236|
237|“딜러, 붙어서 썰어!”
238|
239|“마법사 대기!”
240|
241|쉬쉬쉬쉭! 퍼걱!
242|
243|- 그아아아아!
244|
245|한쪽 팔과 다리를 잃은 트롤의 몸뚱이가 뒤로 쓰러졌다.
246|
247|곧이어 예리한 할버드(Halberd)의 도끼날이 지방과 근육으로 똘똘 뭉친 놈의 목을 갈랐다.
248|
249|쿵! 서걱!
250|
251|어깨 위가 허전해진 트롤의 신형이 퍼덕거렸다. 이내 상처 단면 위로 새로운 살이 꾸물꾸물 차오르기 시작했다.
252|
253|이제 1분 남짓 정도가 흐르면 놈은 새로운 목을 갖게 될 것이다.
254|
255|물론 그때까지 기다리고 있을 스타 길드원들이 아니었다.
256|
257|“지져!”
258|
259|화르르륵! 스아아악!
260|
261|뼛속까지 얼리는 냉기와 살갗을 태우는 화염.
262|
263|재생에 실패한 트롤의 몸뚱이는 한차례 부르르 떨리더니 이내 다시 움직이지 못했다.
264|
265|“3조 클리어!”
266|
267|“여기 도와! 이놈 재생한다!”
268|
269|3인 1개 조로 상대하니 상황은 빠르게 종료됐다.
270|
271|살과 지방이 타들어 가는 악취 속, 십여 미터 떨어진 곳에서 전투를 지켜보던 원명훈이 중얼거렸다.
272|
273|전투의 소음 때문에 아무도 알아들을 수 없을 만큼 작은 목소리였지만 내게는 바로 옆에서 말하는 것처럼 또렷하다.
274|
275|“자식들이 꼭 냄새나게. 웬만하면 얼리라니까.”
276|
277|“허.”
278|
279|나는 새어 나오려는 헛웃음을 간신히 참았다.
280|
281|누가 그런 말을 했었다. 인생은 가까이서 보면 비극이고 멀리서 보면 희극이라고.
282|
283|하지만 몬스터와의 전투는 어디에서 보나 비극이다.
284|
285|한순간에 목숨을 잃을 수 있는 상황, 트롤 살 타는 냄새 정도쯤은 아무것도 아니다.
286|
287|‘병풍 뒤에서 향 타는 냄새 맡는 것보다는 백 배 나으니까.’
288|
289|하지만 원명훈에게는 남의 일일 뿐이었다.
290|
291|이마를 찌푸린 채 작은 목소리로 욕을 내뱉던 그가 문득 시선을 느끼고 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
292|
293|“어, 태경아.”
294|
295|따뜻한 목소리, 언제 그랬냐는 듯 매끈하게 펴진 이마.
296|
297|모든 것이 자연스러웠고, 그래서 더 비정상적으로 느껴졌다.
298|
299|“왜, 무슨 할 말이라도 있어?”
300|
301|‘혹시 내가 한 말 다 듣고 있었냐?’로 들리는 건 어째서인지 모르겠다.
302|
303|나는 내색하지 않고 태연하게 대답했다.
304|
305|“네.”
306|
307|“그래? 뭔데?”
308|
309|“속이 좀 메슥거려서요. 처음에는 괜찮았는데…… 이상하게 여기 들어온 후부터 좀 그래요. 치료 마법도 받아 봤는데 별로 나아지질 않네요.”
310|
311|“아. 그거.”
312|
313|원명훈이 피식 웃었다.
314|
315|“넌 A급 게이트가 처음이라 그런 거야. 게이트 내부에 분포된 마력의 양이 차원이 다르니까.”
316|
317|“아하.”
318|
319|“초보들은 원래 다들 그래. 나야 뭐, 익숙하지.”
320|
321|이미 다 아는 사실이지만, 난생처음 들어 봤다는 듯 탄성을 흘렸다.
322|
323|“그럼 저도 다음에는 좀 익숙해지겠죠?”
324|
325|“다음?”
326|
327|입꼬리를 실룩거리던 원명훈이 고개를 끄덕였다.
328|
329|“그렇지. 다음번에는 훨씬 더 익숙해지겠지.”
330|
331|“그때도 형이랑 함께 왔으면 좋겠네요.”
332|
333|“글쎄, 나도 언제 다시 시간이 될지 모르겠다. 워낙 다른 스케줄이 많아서.”
334|
335|“레이드 뛸 시간도 없으세요?”
336|
337|“태경이 너는 아직 모르겠지만 형 같은 길드장들은 다 바빠. 전반적으로 길드를 조율해야 하거든.”
338|
339|“아아.”
340|
341|“연주자와 지휘자의 차이라고 할까. 마에스트로 알지?”
342|

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 218

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃218화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“이건…….”
  6|
  7|[예티의 목걸이]를 건네받아 살펴보기를 한참, 최 팀장의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.
  8|
  9|“화가 나는군요.”
 10|
 11|평소 이렇게까지 노골적인 감정 표현을 하지 않는 그다.
 12|
 13|가만히 쭈그리고 있던 임꺽정이 잔뜩 궁금한 표정으로 물었다.
 14|
 15|“최 팀장, 왜 그래? 무슨 문제라도 있어?”
 16|
 17|“있습니다. 커다란 문제가.”
 18|
 19|입술을 질끈 깨문 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
 20|
 21|“이 아름다운 제품의 공급이 적다는 것. 이것이야말로 전 세계인에게 지탄받아 마땅한 가장 큰 문제죠.”
 22|
 23|“……아.”
 24|
 25|“보십시오. 고드름을 표현한 이 예술적인 자태를! 설원의 냉기를 고스란히 간직한 마법 기능을!”
 26|
 27|북한 TV 아나운서처럼 열렬하게 수령님, 아니 목걸이를 찬양하던 최 팀장이 나를 향해 고개를 홱 돌렸다.
 28|
 29|“진태경 씨는 어떻게 생각하십니까?”
 30|
 31|“저요?”
 32|
 33|어디서부터 어떻게, 그리고 뭐라 말해야 할까.
 34|
 35|고민은 짧았다. 나 자신도 놀랄 만큼 침착하고 부드러운 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 36|
 37|“저도 화가 나네요.”
 38|
 39|“…….”
 40|
 41|“왜 그러세요?”
 42|
 43|“아닙니다, 그냥.”
 44|
 45|묘한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 최 팀장이 말을 이었다.
 46|
 47|“왠지 좀. 낯선 느낌이 들어서요.”
 48|
 49|“그래요?”
 50|
 51|턱을 문질렀다. 슬슬 고개를 내밀기 시작한 수염이 까슬까슬하다. 그 감촉이 마치 남의 살처럼 낯설었다.
 52|
 53|“면도를 안 해서 그런가.”
 54|
 55|“진태경 씨, 혹시…….”
 56|
 57|최 팀장이 뭐라 말하려던 그때, 원명훈이 사람 좋은 웃음을 지으며 다가왔다.
 58|
 59|“이야, 대단한데. 태경이 너, 진짜 잘 싸우더라.”
 60|
 61|“……그래요?”
 62|
 63|“창술 보니까 내가 만든 교본이랑은 완전히 딴판이던데. 훈련소에서 배운 거야?”
 64|
 65|“아뇨. 그냥 이것저것.”
 66|
 67|“이것저것? 그 정도 수준이 아니던데, 뭘. 이거 몇 년 후면 너한테 따라잡히는 거 아닌지 모르겠다. 하하.”
 68|
 69|나는 말 없이 입꼬리를 끌어 올렸다.
 70|
 71|아무도 따라 웃지 않자 웃음소리는 천천히 사그라졌다. 무안할 법도 한데, 원명훈은 자연스럽게 화제를 돌렸다.
 72|
 73|그런 일련의 모습들이 TV 속 드라마 장면처럼 군더더기 없이 매끄러웠다.
 74|

They could regrow severed arms and legs in a matter of seconds, which naturally made them difficult opponents.

[P93]
But the Star Guild members were seasoned veterans in their own right.

[P94]
“The head! Aim for the head!”

[P95]
“Fire magic!”

[P96]
Sshhk! Fwoooosh!

[P97]
In the early days of the Great Cataclysm, Trolls had earned a fearsome reputation as immortal monsters, but their weaknesses had soon been exposed.

[P98]
*The head and the heart. And magic on top of that.*

[P99]
Unless it was an undead monster, anything died once its life was extinguished.

[P100]
Trolls possessed enough terrifying regenerative power to restore even their heads and hearts, but that didn’t make them truly immortal.

[P101]
Freeze them with ice or sear them with flames before they could regenerate, and there was little they could do.

[P102]
“Damage dealers, get in there and carve it up!”

[P103]
“Mages, stand by!”

[P104]
Sshh-shh-shhk! Thwack!

[P105]

[P106]

[P107]
Thud! Sshhk!

[P108]
The headless Troll thrashed on the ground. Soon, new flesh began to writhe and swell across the severed stump.

[P109]
In about a minute, it would have a new neck.

[P110]
Of course, the Star Guild members had no intention of waiting that long.

[P111]
“Burn it!”

[P112]
Fwoooosh! Ssssss!

[P113]
Bone-chilling cold and skin-scorching flames struck the body.

[P114]
Unable to regenerate, the Troll shuddered violently once, then fell still.

[P115]
“Unit Three clear!”

[P116]
“Help over here! This one’s regenerating!”

[P117]
With three Hunters assigned to each Troll, the battle ended quickly.

[P118]
Amid the stench of burning flesh and fat, Won Myunghoon watched from a dozen or so meters away and muttered under his breath.

[P119]
His voice was too quiet for anyone to hear over the din of battle, but to me, it sounded as clear as if he were standing right beside me.

[P120]
“Idiots had to stink up the place. I told them to freeze them whenever possible.”

[P121]
“Hah.”

[P122]
I barely managed to suppress the incredulous laugh trying to escape.

[P123]
Someone once said that life was a tragedy up close and a comedy from a distance.

[P124]
But a battle against monsters was a tragedy no matter where you watched it from.

[P125]
When one mistake could cost you your life, the smell of burning Troll flesh was nothing.

[P126]
*It’s a hundred times better than lying behind a folding screen, smelling your own funeral incense.*

[P127]
But to Won Myunghoon, it was someone else’s problem.

[P128]
He was frowning and cursing under his breath when he suddenly sensed my gaze and turned toward me.

[P129]
“Oh, Taekyung.”

[P130]
His voice was warm, and his forehead had smoothed out as if nothing had happened.

[P131]
Everything about him seemed perfectly natural.

[P132]
That only made it feel even more unnatural.

[P133]
“What is it? Do you have something to say?”

[P134]
For some reason, it sounded like he was really asking, *Did you hear everything I said?*

[P135]
I kept my face blank and answered casually.

[P136]
“Yes.”

[P137]
“Really? What is it?”

[P138]
“I feel a little nauseous. I was fine at first, but… I’ve felt strange ever since we entered the Gate. I even tried healing magic, but it didn’t help much.”

[P139]
“Ah. That.”

[P140]
Won Myunghoon let out a quiet laugh.

[P141]
“It’s because this is your first A-Rank Gate. The amount of mana inside is on a completely different level.”

[P142]
“Oh, I see.”

[P143]
“Beginners are all like that. I’m used to it by now.”

[P144]
I made a sound of wonder as though I were hearing this for the first time, even though I already knew.

[P145]
“So I’ll be more used to it next time, right?”

[P146]
“Next time?”

[P147]
The corners of Won Myunghoon’s mouth twitched before he nodded.

[P148]
“That’s right. You’ll be much more used to it next time.”

[P149]
“I hope I can come with you again then, hyung.”

[P150]
“Well, I don’t know when I’ll have time. My schedule is packed.”

[P151]
“You don’t even have time for raids?”

[P152]
“You may not know this yet, Taekyung, but Guild Masters like me are always busy. We have to coordinate the entire Guild.”

[P153]
“Ah.”

[P154]
“It’s the difference between a musician and a conductor. You know what a maestro is, right?”

[P155]
As Won Myunghoon mimed waving a conductor’s baton, I abruptly asked, “Then did you go to the department store for a Guild-related meeting?”

[P156]
“Hm?”

[P157]
“I saw an article about it online. What was the headline again? Ah, I remember.”

[P158]
Won Myunghoon was momentarily at a loss for words. Looking straight at him, I carefully recited it.

[P159]
“Something like *Rising Star Hunter Won Myunghoon Sweeps Up Luxury Goods.*”

[P160]
“…There was an article like that?”

[P161]
“It was on a Hunter community site for a little while. It got deleted after five minutes.”

[P162]
“R-really? Are you sure you didn’t misread it?”

[P163]
“Yes. There’s a Rice Weevil who doesn’t study these days and does nothing but scour the Internet. He lets me know the moment an article appears.”

[P164]
A deep dimple formed in Won Myunghoon’s handsome face. But this wasn’t the bright smile I remembered seeing on television.

[P165]
“That can’t be right.”

[P166]
“Of course not.”

[P167]
“I mean, I do like shopping, but not that much. I go once a month at most.”

[P168]
“I heard there were pictures too.”

[P169]
“…”

[P170]
“You know Dispass, right? The site that specializes in digging up dirt on celebrities. They even interviewed someone from the department store. Apparently, you’re a VVIP who visits five times a week.”

[P171]
“…”

[P172]
Won Myunghoon licked his dry lips. The dimple had vanished without a trace.

[P173]
“Taekyung. You don’t actually believe that, do you?”

[P174]
“Come on, it must be a rumor-sheet story. You’re far too busy coordinating the Guild’s schedule, hyung. Maestro.”

[P175]
“…Right. Maestro.”

[P176]
I vigorously mimed waving a conductor’s baton while Won Myunghoon stared at me with dry eyes.

[P177]
That was when—

[P178]
“Hyung! No, CEO!”

[P179]
The shout rang out across the endless wasteland of dirt, sand, and winding rocky hills. It had come from Star Guild’s Team Leader 1.

[P180]
He had gone scouting in search of the Wyvern that had been nowhere in sight, and now he was back.

[P181]
But unlike when he had set out at a leisurely pace, he was sprinting toward us like a madman, his face deathly pale.

[P182]
“What happened? Where are the others?”

[P183]
At Won Myunghoon’s question, Team Leader 1 stammered.

[P184]
“Th-they, th-that…”

[P185]
I didn’t need to hear the rest.

[P186]
Seven people had left, but only one had returned. The drops of blood spattered across his face and armor turned my suspicions into certainty.

[P187]
“You bastard. Spit it out!”

[P188]
Team Leader 1 flinched at the thunderous roar.

[P189]
“We found a Wyvern.”

[P190]
“A Wyvern? How many?”

[P191]
“O-one.”

[P192]
“What? One?”

[P193]
An A-Rank Hunter and six B-Rank Hunters were more than capable of dealing with a single Wyvern.

[P194]
Yet six of them had died, while only one had escaped.

[P195]
“You call that an explanation? Are you fucking with me?”

[P196]
“They’re all dead. We approached under concealment magic, but… it noticed us.”

[P197]
“What kind of bullshit is that? How could a Wyvern see through concealment magic?”

[P198]
Click. Clack-clack.

[P199]
His teeth chattered in terror. At last, Team Leader 1 forced out the words.

[P200]
“A-A Named Monster.”

[P201]
“…!”

[P202]
“It’s definitely a Named Monster. This place… is a Mutated Gate.”

[P203]
An A-Rank Mutated Gate.

[P204]
And a Named Monster.

[P205]
There wasn’t a single person among us who didn’t understand what those two terms meant.

[P206]
Amid the suffocating silence, someone muttered in a voice barely loud enough to hear.

[P207]
“Fuck…”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
